title: Opportunity Flow: RICE+Elasticity Prioritization Framework
creator: Aisha N. Carter
description: Introduce a hybrid prioritization method called Opportunity Flow that augments classic RICE scoring with workload-specific elasticity signals (cost per token elasticity, tail latency risk) and a velocity multiplier to reflect engineering cost-of-delay. The goal is to make prioritization for inference-related initiatives (runtime, routing, console features) explicitly reflect production economics and rollout velocity, enabling coherent quarterly planning and OKR alignment.
proposal_summary: Opportunity Flow = (RICE_score) * ElasticityFactor * VelocityMultiplier. RICE_score uses conventional Reach, Impact, Confidence, Effort. ElasticityFactor compresses cost/latency benefits into a single multiplier (TokenDollar ROI and TailLatency Risk). VelocityMultiplier discounts initiatives with high engineering wait/operational overhead or increases score for small, high-velocity wins. Use this composite score to rank roadmap candidates and to identify projects that shift unit economics vs. pure feature value.
scoring_components: Reach: estimate number of active requests/users affected per month (numeric estimate mapped to buckets)
Impact: expected improvement on primary metric (0.25, 0.5, 1.0, 2.0 scale depending on magnitude)
Effort: engineering person-months (converted to points for consistency)
TokenDollar ROI: estimated $ saved per million tokens after change (positive for savings, negative for added cost)
TailLatency Risk: qualitative multiplier (0.8-1.2) capturing probability & severity of increasing 95/99th latency
VelocityMultiplier: 0.5-1.5 factor to model time-to-value and operational friction (smaller, faster projects get >1)
calculation_notes: RICE_score = (Reach * Impact * Confidence) / Effort. ElasticityFactor = 1 + normalize(TokenDollar ROI) - risk_penalty(TailLatency). VelocityMultiplier applied last. Normalization functions and thresholds live in the Roadmap Prioritization spreadsheet (linked in comments).
worked_example: Reach = 120k requests/month (bucket -> 3), Impact = 0.8 (reduces token generation by 12%), Confidence = 60 (0.6), Effort = 2 person-months
TokenDollar ROI = $250 per million tokens saved -> normalize to +0.12 ElasticityFactor contribution
Opportunity Flow score = 0.72 * 1.10 * 1.2 = 0.95 (use for ranked listing; also compute cost impact separately)
acceptance_criteria: Framework documented in Confluence with normalization tables and calculation spreadsheet link
Scoring automation prototype integrated into internal roadmap spreadsheet (CSV export + one-click rank)
Three pilot initiatives scored and validated with cross-functional stakeholders (ENG, Design, Finance)
Playbook for resolving ties and adjusting VelocityMultiplier accepted by PM leadership
Rollout plan for Q2 includes training session and a review checkpoint after first cycle
rollout_plan: Week 1: Finalize normalization thresholds and publish Confluence guide
Week 2: Implement scoring columns in centralized Roadmap sheet; wiring for auto-calculation
Week 3: Run pilot with 3 initiatives: one runtime, one console, one dedicated-product feature
Week 4: Collect feedback, adjust elastic normalization and velocity rules
Week 5: Present to GTM + Eng leadership and adopt for Cycle 2025-W12 planning
open_questions: How do we reconcile TokenDollar ROI estimates with engineering-reported effort when both are uncertain?
Should TailLatency Risk be applied per-customer segment (enterprise vs self-serve) or globally?
What guardrails prevent gaming the VelocityMultiplier? (proposal: require engineering sign-off + historical velocity calibration)
Do we surface cost savings as a separate ranking column for sales/finance conversations?
